traits: Cap 5 to 10 cm, convex then spreading, with a central boss; whitish ochre to reddish, paler at the margin; sticky in damp weather
Fairly close, toothed gills, whitish then brown; in damp weather they weep brownish drops
Stem 5 to 10 cm, whitish, rust-stained towards the base, slightly swollen below, frosted over a good length; no ring
Fairly thick white flesh · distinct smell of radish, bitter taste
Fairly common in summer and autumn, under broadleaves or conifers, in groups along paths and ditches, in lawns
safetyNote: Toxic: digestive upset, from mild to marked (nausea, vomiting, diarrhoea, cramps) (Wikipedia EN). The German mycological society lists the whole Hebeloma genus among the gastrointestinal-syndrome mushrooms, and the Belgian poison centre cites the poison pie among the causes of the mild resinoid syndrome: moderate gastroenteritis, less than 3 hours after the meal, lasting under 12 hours. The risk is confusion with tricholomas (Wikipedia FR): the radish smell and the browning gills help to recognise it.
